title: Quotes on the Move

intro.quote: “Anything with too heavy data is not pure responsive … is it really needed to show the editor as it is, or is it better to show the PDF preview and only when they need to edit they click Edit? Mobile and tablet need to be an on-the-move experience, not like the desktop.”
intro.method: A read-only audit of every Quotes screen at 390 (phone), 768 (tablet, portrait) and 1024 (tablet, landscape), with touch emulation, on a production build of today’s main. Three lanes measured touch boxes, type sizes, truncation and sideways scroll and read the code behind each screen. Nothing is built yet. Your picks save as you make them.
answer: Yes: on a phone a quote should open as the document, and the editor should come only on Edit. Today the phone gets the desktop page folded into one scroll: a five-row header, an eight-card form, the Items as cards, the Preview as an A4 page shrunk to 310px that nobody can read. On a tablet the Items grid keeps all its columns at 768 and truncates the ones that matter.

The good news: the pieces for the right experience already exist. The client’s confirmation page is the model (one total, one action, then the lines as readable cards), the Items cards (REG-597) and the line sheet are built, the Send sheet is right. What changes is the order of what a designer meets, and the sizes.

proposalTitle: The proposal: a quote you read first and edit second
proposalIntro: Six rules, then the screens drawn with OpenMaison’s own tokens, then each change as a card you can mark. Desktop stays exactly as mocked; the data, rules and flows are the same code behind a different order of screens.

principles.title: Read first, edit second
principles.body: A quote opens as the document the client gets, with its status, amount and validity on top. Edit is a deliberate step, never the default.

principles.title: One primary per screen
principles.body: The filled button is the one thing this state needs next (Send · Remind · Mark signed · Open the contract). Everything else sits behind ⋮ or in a sheet.

principles.title: One thing at a time
principles.body: Editing is a list of sections, each its own screen, instead of eight cards in one scroll. Each row says what is inside so most never need opening.

principles.title: The numbers are big, the fields are few
principles.body: Amounts at 18–26px, body 16px, secondary 14px, nothing under 14px on site. Five fields a thumb can change on site; the other eleven one tap further.

principles.title: Nothing is lost, it is one tap further
principles.body: Every desktop action stays reachable on a phone. Rare things move behind ⋮; frequent things come to the thumb.

principles.title: A tablet is not a small desktop
principles.body: Portrait follows the phone with room for two columns; landscape holds the document beside one pane. The grid shows four editable columns, never twelve.

proposals.title: A quote opens as its document on a phone and a tablet
proposals.today: Opening a quote lands on the editor: a five-row header (title, three chips, Saved, the status dropdown and Send), the tabs row, then General Info, Items, Payment Schedule, Files, Terms, Notes, Signature and Activity as cards in one scroll of about 6,000px. A Signed quote opens on the same editable form with a dead lilac Send button.
proposals.proposed: A Quote screen: back · client name · ⋮; a hero with the status chip, the amount, validity and lines, and the client’s name with Call and WhatsApp; one “Next” line that says what this state needs; the document as reading cards (the confirmation page’s own component); a sticky foot with Edit and the state’s one primary (Send ▾). Nothing on this screen edits; it reads and acts.
proposals.why: the person opening a quote at a site or in a car wants to know where it stands and do one thing. The editor is for the desk. The confirmation page already proves the reading layout works at 390; the hero and the foot are the house pieces.

proposals.title: Edit is a list of sections, each a screen
proposals.today: Every section is a card on one page. To change the validity date you scroll past Items and Payments; the tabs row only jumps the scroll.
proposals.proposed: Edit quote opens a list: General info · Items (16) · Payment schedule · Files (1) · Terms and conditions · Additional notes · Signature, each with a one-line summary of what is inside. A row opens that section as a full-screen sheet with Done; the dock steps back while editing. On a tablet the list is the left pane and the open section the right.
proposals.why: one question per screen is the whole difference between a phone and a desk. The summaries mean most sections are never opened, and the ones that are never scroll past their Done.

proposals.title: The Items cards grow up: bigger names, kind on the line, sticky total, a foot with Add
proposals.today: REG-597’s cards work, but the name clips at two lines and 14px, the kind (Labour · Purchase) is hidden, the section head scrolls away, the Add Item button is a small + in the card’s head, and the total is in the summary at the bottom of the page.
proposals.proposed: Name at 15px that wraps; the quantity line reads “44 sqft × S$102 · Purchase”; a tap on a section card folds it (its sheet is behind ⋮ › Edit section); the section head is tinted and sticks while its lines scroll; depth drawn with a left bar, not a margin; the screen head shows “16 lines · S$49,838” and stays; a foot with Add section and + Add item (48px). The totals are a pinned strip (Subtotal · GST · Total) with Adjust for entity, discounts and GST and Breakdown for By category. The row ⋮ is five rows (Duplicate · Mark as optional · Move to section › · Remove · More…); the bulk bar is the count + Clear, then Move · Delete · ⋯. Column settings, Row density and Expand don’t appear on a phone.
proposals.why: on site the job is to add a line, change a number and see the total move; today each of those is two to four taps and a long scroll.

proposals.title: The line sheet in two layers: five fields first, the rest under More
proposals.today: The line sheet lists every column the grid has (sixteen fields) in one scroll; Done is below the fold and the quantity opens the full keyboard.
proposals.proposed: Item name · Quantity · Unit · Unit price · Kind, then a computed Total, then one row More: description, cost and markup, print as, room, link… that opens the rest. Numeric keypad for quantity and price; Delete and Done always visible.
proposals.why: the five fields are what changes at a client’s home; cost and markup are desk work and should not sit between a thumb and Done.

proposals.title: “As printed” is a viewer, not the main screen
proposals.today: The Preview page draws the A4 at 310px wide at 390: 4px type, no zoom, five controls stacked in the header (Internal copy, What your client sees, Copy link, Download PDF, Send) before the first page.
proposals.proposed: On a phone, Preview shows the client’s reflowed quote (the reading cards the confirmation page already draws at 390) under one 56px bar (Back · Preview · Send), with Paper as a toggle that opens the A4 as a viewer: fit to width, pinch to zoom, swipe between pages with page dots, Download in the bar. Copy link (“team only”), Share PDF, Internal copy, What your client sees and Change template move under ⋮. On a tablet the paper renders at its text width (zoom 1, the margins scrolling), so 768 reads. The editor’s Client view button at ≤1024 opens this Preview; the 400px drawer stays desktop-only.
proposals.why: the paper is for checking the print, a few times a month; what a designer shows a client on a phone is the quote, and it has to read without a pinch.

proposals.title: The list card: who, how much, what is waiting
proposals.today: The card (REG-377) carries a checkbox, the title, number · Shared · client, a status dropdown, the amount and ⋮. The client’s name is the third thing on the card; “Expired 16 Sep” is red but says nothing about what to do.
proposals.proposed: The client’s name leads, the amount is big and right, the second line is number · title, and the status is a chip with its “since” beside it (“Sent to client · opened 3 Oct · expires in 4 days”). The dropdown, the checkbox and Shared/Private leave the card: the status changes on the quote, a long-press selects, Shared shows as a small lock on the chip only when private.
proposals.why: a designer thinks “Serena’s quote”, not “OM-10007”; and the card’s job is to say which quote needs them today.

proposals.title: Tablet: the Items grid shows four editable columns; the rest opens in a pane
proposals.today: At 768 and 1024 the full desktop grid renders (drag handle, +, checkbox, #, Item, Type, Qty, Unit, Unit price, Total, ⋮ …) in a sideways scroller with a frozen first block. Item names truncate (“Hacking of existin…”), Type reads “Purcha”, and editing a cell needs a keyboard and a steady hand on a 20px target.
proposals.proposed: At 768 portrait: the phone’s cards with a 400px line panel beside them, so the list stays in view while a line is edited (Qty and Unit price first). At 1024 landscape: a working grid — Item · Qty · Unit · Unit price · Total (642px in a 902px card, no pan), edited in place with 44px cells, sections as tinted rows with “+ Add to …” under each; the other columns behind Column settings remembered per breakpoint; tapping a line opens the rest in the pane. The head’s “internal” meaning gets a visible caption on touch. No sideways scroll on any tablet width; Expand goes.
proposals.why: a tablet on site is a bigger phone, not a smaller desk: the twelve-column grid was designed for a mouse and a 1440 screen, and at 768 it leaves a 62px slit to edit through.

proposals.title: One scale for the phone and the touch tablet: 16 · 14 · 44
proposals.today: Body text in the editor is 14px and some captions 12px; several targets are under 44px (measured per screen below); amounts are the same size as labels.
proposals.proposed: A phone type scale for the Quotes screens: body 16, secondary 14, amounts 18–26 tabular; every target 44px, foot buttons 48; 16px gutters, 12px inside cards. Applied through the existing media queries, so desktop stays byte-identical.
proposals.why: a world-class phone screen is first a readable one; the numbers are the point of a quote.

proposals.title: The header on a phone is one line plus the state
proposals.today: Title with a rename chevron, ⋮, ✕; three chips; a Saved line; the status dropdown beside Send; then the tabs: five rows, about 230px, before anything of the quote.
proposals.proposed: With P-01 the editor’s header on a phone is: ✕ · “Edit quote” with the number and Saved as the sub-line · Done. The status and Send live on the Quote screen; the chips (version, contract) become one line in the hero.
proposals.why: the header should cost one row; the state belongs where the actions are.

proposals.title: Create Quote on a phone: four big rows, templates behind one
proposals.today: The sheet shows the template gallery as a two-column grid of thumbnails (names truncate to “Defa…”) above the three other ways to start, so the most common choice (the default template) competes with the others.
proposals.proposed: Studio-wide, a first step on its own: “Who is this quote for?” (the lead picker, recent leads first), so nothing can be refused silently. Then four rows at 56px: Default template (its full name, “Starts with …”, with “change” to pick another), Blank quote, Upload a quote (opens the files / camera sheet at once), Draft with Maison AI. The gallery opens from “change”; the picker’s list view is fixed (A-12).
proposals.why: on a phone a choice is a list, not a gallery; the default is right nine times in ten; and a refused tap must say why.

proposals.title: Tablet lists: a default column set with the row’s ⋮ frozen
proposals.today: At 768 the Quotes table is 2,108px wide (3.3 screens): Title · Client · Status · Creator fill the first screen, the Total starts off-screen, and the row’s View + ⋮ sit 1,466px to the right. At 1024 the Total is cut mid-figure. On the lead’s Quotes tab the quick-links strip takes another 72px, so the table has 570.
proposals.proposed: At ≤1024 on touch the tables open with a tablet default set — Title · Client · Status · Total · Due — with Title and ⋮ frozen, View dropped (the title opens), the rest kept in Column settings. The lead tab hides the quick-links strip at 768 portrait as it does on a phone. The to-do chip keeps its words at every width.
proposals.why: a column set chosen per browser (REG-454) won’t be set by a studio of ten; the first screen has to carry the amount and the actions by default.

proposals.title: The client’s confirmation page: read first, then a sticky Confirm
proposals.today: The Confirm card (name field, Confirm quote, Ask for a change) is the first screen; the 19 lines follow for 2,100px and end with no Confirm in reach. The buttons are 36px. A tablet gets the A4 at 10px type with the reading cards hidden; the phone’s “View as printed” draws the A4 at 4px inline.
proposals.proposed: A total card (“S$88,704.75 · 19 lines · valid until 16 Sep” + View as printed), then the reading cards, then a sticky bottom bar at every scroll: Confirm quote (48px) and Ask. Confirm opens a short sheet (name, the one line of fine print, Confirm). Cards at ≤1024 portrait; the paper beside the card only in landscape. “As printed” opens full-screen with pinch.
proposals.why: the homeowner is always on a phone, usually from a WhatsApp link; the page’s own words say “please read the quote” and then put Confirm first. The signing page already has this sticky bar.
shots: The end of the quote · no Confirm · 390

findingsTitle: What is wrong today, screen by screen
findingsNote: most are covered by the proposal above; the rest are quick fixes you can pick
findingsIntro: Each finding names what was seen, where, and how bad. A finding the proposal already resolves says so and needs no pick. Severity: Blocker = can’t finish the job at that width · Major = slow or error-prone · Minor = polish.

surfaces.title: Tools › Quotes and the lead’s Quotes tab
surfaces.intro: The list is the phone’s best surface in the module (cards since REG-377), which is why its gaps show: the card was drawn before Due, Valid until and Viewed existed, and the tablet keeps the desktop table.

findings.title: The card’s second line clips, and the client’s name is what goes
findings.what: “OM-10008 · Private · Expired 21 Sep ’26 · Vivien Lee” is cut with no ellipsis on three of seven cards (322–344px of text in a 248px box). Every demo title is “Whole-home renovation”, so the client is the only thing that tells the cards apart.
findings.absorbedNote: the client leads the card

findings.title: The only way to open a quote is its 14px title
findings.what: A 248×20 touch box; the rest of the card is inert and the ⋮ sheet has no Open row (View is hidden on a phone).
findings.absorbedNote: the whole card is the press, with a chevron

findings.title: The card’s biggest control changes the status
findings.what: A 96–139 × 44 bordered pill opens a six-row write menu (Draft … Signed), every row enabled even on a Signed quote. One mis-tap in a car opens a sheet whose first row is Draft.
findings.absorbedNote: a read-only chip; Change status in the ⋮ (Q-04)

findings.title: No date reaches the phone card
findings.what: Due, Valid until, Sent, Created and Viewed are all hidden on the card; the only time signal is a red “Expired 16 Sep ’26”. On the move the question is “sent when, viewed yet, due when”.
findings.absorbedNote: the third line says it

findings.title: The Maison AI button covers the amount
findings.what: The FAB (326–374 × 710–758) sits over card 4’s S$88,705 at rest; with a selection it rises and covers the next card’s figure.
findings.absorbedNote: the amount moves to the title line, right

findings.title: On a tablet the row’s View + ⋮ are 1.2–1.5 screens to the right
findings.what: The 150px actions band (REG-310, an in-flow band on touch) starts at x = 2,063 inside a 642px frame at 768; nothing on the first screen says a row has actions.

findings.title: The amount is not on the tablet’s first screen
findings.what: At 768 the Total column starts at x = 918 in a frame that ends at 736; at 1024 it is cut mid-figure, “S$62,70”.

findings.title: The lead’s Quotes tab at 768 is 35% chrome before its one card
findings.what: The quick-links strip (72) + the rail (60) + gutters leave the tab 570px; the table is 1,928px (3.4 screens) and the tabs row scrolls with no pager cue.
findings.absorbedNote: the strip hides at 768 portrait

findings.title: The to-do chip reads “⌛ 3” on a tablet
findings.what: The words “Waiting on client” live only in aria-label; on touch there is no tooltip, and pressed it reads “⌛ 3 ✕” with nothing saying what the list is narrowed to. The bar’s left half is empty.
findings.fix: Keep the chip’s words at ≤1024; use the short form only when the toolbar measures that they don’t fit (as the Tasks page does).

findings.title: A typed search pushes the toolbar 8px off the screen
findings.what: With text typed the clear ✕ widens the field (210 → 238) and the ⋮ lands at 362–398, clipped.
findings.fix: `min-width: 0` on the search box so it gives way, or fold the ⋮ while the box is open.

findings.title: Selection on the phone offers only Delete
findings.what: A 44px checkbox on every card for a destructive-only bulk bar, which lands on the fourth card’s status pill.
findings.absorbedNote: no checkbox; a long-press selects

findings.title: Filters is the desktop two-pane modal inside a sheet
findings.what: A 156px rail + a 218px pane inside a 401px sheet: five tabs, each a press, then Done. The common asks (status, due, valid until) are one chip row each.
findings.fix: One scrolling sheet with sections on the house Chips (Status · Due · Valid until · Dates · Sort).

findings.title: Column settings on touch: 24px drag handles, and none on a phone
findings.what: Row order by pointer-dragging 24px handles in a 400px drawer; the drawer is not offered ≤767, so nothing the phone card hides can be chosen there.
findings.absorbedNote: the tablet default makes it rare; the phone card decides for itself

surfaces.title: The client’s pages
surfaces.intro: The homeowner is always on a phone. The confirmation page’s reading cards are the best phone pattern in the module; the page around them was laid out for a desk.

findings.title: Confirm comes before the quote, and never again after it
findings.what: The Confirm card (442px) is the first screen; the 19 lines run from y 542 to 2,671 and end at the Terms table with no Confirm in reach. The card’s own words say “please read the quote”.

findings.title: A tablet gets the A4 only, at 10px type
findings.what: At 768 the print is drawn at 0.885 scale (body 10.1px, smallest 7.3px); the reading cards exist in the DOM but are hidden ≥768, and there is no “View as a list”.

findings.title: The page’s one action is 36px tall
findings.what: “Confirm quote” 324×36, “Ask for a change” 36, “View as printed” 36; the name field types at 14px on Android. The client pages carry no touch rule at all.

findings.title: “View as printed” draws the A4 inline at 4px
findings.what: Scale 0.438: lines 5px, the smallest text 3.6px; pinching zooms the whole page.

surfaces.title: The editor’s frame: header, tabs, Send, ⋮ and the banners
surfaces.intro: The desktop header stacked into five rows, a tab strip that scrolls with no cue, and a Send button that leaves on the first scroll: this is where the “squeezed, not designed” feeling starts. P-01, P-02 and P-09 replace the frame on a phone; the quick fixes below stand on their own.

findings.title: The one primary action scrolls away
findings.what: At ≤767 the header leaves the sticky stack and only the 48px tab row holds. The Draft page is 6,832px tall as loaded (8,646 with every section open), so from Signature or Activity, Send and the status pill are about 6,000px up.
findings.absorbedNote: the Quote screen’s sticky foot holds Send; the editor’s header is one row (P-09)

findings.title: 184px of header, 424px of chrome on a Sent quote, before the first field
findings.what: Title 24 + four 10px chips wrapping to two lines (44) + Saved 20 + the status/Send row 36 + gaps; with the tabs 232px. On the Sent quote the 192px banner makes it 424px, half the screen.

findings.title: The Sent banner is six lines of 14px with its button on a seventh
findings.what: 192px (50 words) on the Sent quote; 112px on Signed. REG-624’s words are a decision; their phone layout is not.
findings.absorbedNote: one line in the hero (“Sent 19 Aug · v1 with the client · validity ended 16 Sep ▾”), Revise inline

findings.title: Five of eight sections are off the tab strip with no cue
findings.what: The strip is 876px in 390: Files, Terms, Notes, Signature and Activity are off-screen with no pager, fade or mask; the cut “Files (” is the only hint. A new user does not know Signature and Activity exist.
findings.absorbedNote: the section list replaces the strip

findings.title: The ⋮ sheet holds 16 rows and still scrolls
findings.what: Version History and Delete are below the fold with no cue; three jobs (see as the client · change the record · get it out) are mixed in one list; keyboard hints (“P”) print on a touch sheet.
findings.absorbedNote: Preview, Client view and Comments move to the Quote screen; the sheet groups the rest (Look · Change · Share · Export) and hides key hints on touch

findings.title: The header chips type at 10px
findings.what: “OM-10001”, “VERSION 1”, “CONTRACT · DRAFT” at 10/12; Saved at 12. REG-344 kept the mobile body at 14, which is a decision; 10px does not read in daylight.
findings.absorbedNote: one 12px line “OM-10001 · Draft · v1”; a chip only for the contract

findings.what: The title button (the lead’s other quotes) is 261×24, the only header control without a 44 overlay.

surfaces.title: The sections: General Info, Payment Schedule, Files, Terms and Notes, Signature, Activity
surfaces.intro: Each desktop card was kept and stacked. One of them cannot be used at all on a phone.

findings.title: On a phone nothing on a payment row can be tapped
findings.what: Every tap on “10%”, the amount, the due date, the description or the red Remove resolves to the drag handle: `.handle::after { position: absolute; inset: -10px }` on a `.handle` that is never positioned, and ≤767 `.cell.cSel { position: static }` lets the overlay span the whole row. A real tap on “10%” opens no editor (it does at 768). The schedule can’t be edited and a payment can’t be removed.
findings.fix: `payments-section.module.css`: `.handle { position: relative }` (the fix REG-729 gave the Cancel / OK buttons), then a real-tap probe. A bug fix, independent of everything else here.

findings.title: At 768 the Payment Schedule cuts its words and overlaps its heads
findings.what: Six tracks in 596px: Description cells are 64px (“Upon sigr”, “Works co”, “50% com”) and the heads read “PERCENTAGE (%AMOUNT (S$)”.

surfaces.title: Items on a phone
surfaces.intro: REG-597’s cards are the right idea. Around them sit the desktop’s menus, bar and summary, and one broken rule puts every touch box 22px up and left of its glyph.

findings.title: Every icon button in the Items module has its 44px touch box displaced by (−22, −22)
findings.what: Three module rules (`item-cards`, `items-table`, `items-section`) override only the edges of the house `.btn::after` overlay, whose translate(−50%, −50%) still applies: a card’s kebab box sits 32px up-left of its glyph with nothing below or right; the toolbar’s Create box covers the right third of the Maison AI glyph; a tap 6px above-left of a section’s fold chevron opened the kebab menu. The DS Button and the sheet close are correct.
findings.fix: Delete the three `inset` overrides; the house `.btn::after` already gives a centred 44. Add a design-lint rule: no `::after { inset … }` on a `.btn`. A bug fix, one change for every Items control at every touch width.

findings.title: The two things a finger does most on a section are its smallest targets
findings.what: The fold chevron (24×24) and the kebab (24×24) sit 2px apart at the card’s edge; with C-03 neither has a usable grown box. The checkbox (44) and the text area (270×82) are right.
findings.absorbedNote: a tap on the card folds it; the ⋮ is the house 36 kebab

questionsIntro: Where the proposal has more than one good answer. My recommendation is marked.

questions.title: Does a tablet in portrait (768) get the phone model or the desktop model?
opts: The phone model with room: the document first, two-column fields, the Items grid at four columns (P-07)
The desktop editor, as today, with the fixes
Phone model up to 1024 in portrait; desktop only on landscape tablets

questions.title: Where does Edit land?
opts: On the section list, every time (predictable)
On the section last edited on this phone
Straight into Items, the most edited section

questions.title: Should a tablet ever show the full desktop grid?
opts: No. Four columns and the pane on every touch tablet; a keyboard-and-mouse tablet at 1025+ gets desktop
Yes, behind a “Full table” switch in the Items ⋮, remembered per device

questions.title: Changing a quote’s status from the list on a phone
opts: Only on the quote (the chip on the card is read-only); fewer accidental changes
Keep the dropdown on the card, as today

questions.title: Hide the bottom dock while editing a quote?
opts: Yes: the dock hides inside Edit and the line sheet, and comes back on Done (focus)
No: the dock stays on every screen

questions.title: What the “As printed” viewer opens at
opts: Fit to width, pinch to zoom
100% scale (readable, scrolls sideways within the viewer)

questions.title: The one primary button per state
questions.note: My proposed mapping: Draft → Send ▾ · Sent for Approval → Approve (approvers) / nothing (others) · Approved → Send ▾ · Sent to Client → Remind · Confirmed → Send for signature · Signed → Open contract / Move to Won · Expired → Revise.
opts: Always Send ▾, as the desktop header does
No primary on the Quote screen; actions only in ⋮

questions.title: After Quotes, which module next?
opts: Lead Details (the most used on site)
